To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce label conditioning that allows us to generate samples of classes that are not in the training set; (2) this allows us to generate maps of emergent features; (3) we also introduce a diversity metric, which gives a quantitative measure of the diversity of samples generated from a class-conditional GAN model.
GANs trained with our method produce samples that are more realistic and diverse than previous methods, and that the diversity of samples is greater than the diversity of real data.

(1) GANs trained by our modified GAN training process achieve state-of-the-art results on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, CelebA, and ImageNet; and (2) ImageNet samples generated with this process are class informative, where class information cannot be inferred from the low resolution 32x32 images that were previously used to evaluate conditional Image synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of how to improve the sample quality of GANs and proposes two approaches in answering it: (a) a large scale GAN training procedure that achieves new sample quality highs of 128x128 images and (b) an analysis of the reliability, reproducibility and the consistency among sample quality scores of the above method and amongst the current state of the art GANs for image generation in general.
